paper.title: An improved Monte Carlo factorization algorithm

program.how: written for ounce-core from the paper's two algorithms (Pollard's rho with Floyd's cycle finding and the product-of-differences trick, and Brent's cycle-finding variant of Section 7 with m = 1), counting multiplications mod N as the paper does; the sequence x0 = 0, f(x) = x^2 + 3 is run modulo the least prime factor p, since a factor p is detected exactly when a term divisible by p enters the product; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: Section 8: for the Floyd-based algorithm the count M_p / sqrt(p) at p = 99,398,833 (the published location of the maximum over odd primes p < 10^8) is 20.3613 to the 4 published decimals
Section 8: for Brent's algorithm the count M_p / sqrt(p) at p = 48,569,393 (the published location of its maximum) is 18.9972 to the 4 published decimals

for all 25996 odd primes p < 300000 neither algorithm's M_p / sqrt(p) exceeds those published maxima, and the means over this smaller sample (4.1334 and 3.1308) are within 1% of the published means 4.122795 and 3.122533 for p < 10^8 (a consistency check only)

expected_values_source.what: Table 8.1 and the accompanying text of the paper (maxima 20.3613 and 18.9972 at p = 99,398,833 and 48,569,393; actual means 4.122795 and 3.122533), copied as numbers; the text was extracted from the author's PDF
expected_values_source.note: the extracted text reads the two algorithm columns of Table 8.1 as P_F' and P_2' (OCR garbled); the exact match of both maxima to 4 decimals with the listings as implemented confirms the reading. The checks at the two primes are exact matches; the scan is only a consistency check

negative_control: built with -DBRENT_C=4 (f(x) = x^2 + 4 instead of x^2 + 3), M_p / sqrt(p) at the two primes is 6.5734 and 2.3660 instead of 20.3613 and 18.9972, and the program exits 1
not_checked: the means and maxima over all 5,761,454 odd primes below 10^8 (about 10^11 multiplications; too slow for the 2 billion instruction default budget): only the two maximum locations and a sample of 25996 primes
factoring an actual composite N with GCDs and multi-word arithmetic: the counts are obtained modulo p
Section 7's variant that omits product terms for k < 3r/2 and the theoretical expectations (7.1)
the period/tail table (Table 2.1) of the calculator generator, whose recurrence is not given
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, reproduces the two maxima in the paper's Table 8.1 to the published 4 decimals by counting multiplications of the two rho variants. It does not show the paper's averages over 10^8 primes.
